sections.h2: Which Fannin County offices handle my property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work, and both sit in the Blue Ridge area. The Fannin County Tax Assessors set values and take exemption paperwork, while the Tax Commissioner sends the bills and collects the money.

The Tax Commissioner's main office is at 400 West Main Street, Suite 103, Blue Ridge, GA 30513, the same street as the county courthouse. Its phone is (706) 632-2645, and the posted hours run Monday through Thursday from 8:30 to 5:00 and Friday from 8:30 to 4:30. The county's own directory lists the Tax Assessor at (706) 632-5954, and the county links to an online parcel search on qPublic.

sections.h2: What does the Fannin County landscape mean for a house sale?
sections.html:
Fannin is a mountain county with a thin settlement pattern. The Census Bureau counts 387.11 square miles of land and 65.4 residents per square mile in 2020, which is far looser than the metro counties to the south. A parcel here is often a few acres on a slope, so access roads, septic systems and well water show up in a buyer's questions early.

The county government publishes a long list of ordinances that touch a house sale, among them a land development ordinance, a building code enforcement ordinance, a dilapidated building ordinance, a manufactured home and trailer ordinance, a septic installation ordinance and a short-term rental ordinance. Before you list a cabin or a lot, read the ordinances that fit your property on the county's ordinance page, and call the building department at (706) 632-8361 with questions about a past permit.

Blue Ridge holds the county courthouse, and the Chattahoochee forest country around it draws visitors. That visitor traffic is why short-term rental rules matter so much in Fannin, and the next sections cover them.

sections.h2: Who lives in Fannin County and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 26,111 residents on July 1, 2025, up 3.1 percent from the 2020 base of 25,331. About one in three residents, 32.2 percent, is 65 or older, the oldest mix among the three counties in the same Census table.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $306,600.
  • Median gross rent: $900 a month.
  • Housing units in 2025: 19,655, against 11,890 households.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 78.6 percent.
  • Persons per household: 2.15.
  • Median household income: $57,073.
  • Building permits in 2025: 356.

Notice the gap between 19,655 housing units and 11,890 households. A large share of Fannin's housing stock is not someone's year-round home, which fits the cabin and vacation market and explains why buyers ask about rental history and lodging tax records.

sections.h2: When is Fannin County property tax due?
sections.html:
Ask the Fannin County Tax Commissioner for the due date printed on your bill, because the state allows each county to choose among several dates. The Georgia Department of Revenue says the default official due date is December 20, and a local government can move it to December 1 or November 15 or split the bill into installments.

State guidance also gives every taxpayer 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest starts, with penalties possible on balances that stay unpaid. Mobile homes follow a separate calendar: a location permit within 30 days of placing the home, then each year between January 1 and April 1, with the return due on or before April 1.

The City of Blue Ridge bills its own tax. According to the city, notices usually go out in November and payment is due within 60 days of the postmark. The city's mayor and council set the city rate, and the city says the Fannin County Tax Assessors produce the values it bills from. If your house is inside the city, you will hold a county bill and a city bill.

sections.h2: How do returns and the homestead exemption work in Fannin County?
sections.html:
Georgia asks owners to file a property return with the county tax office between January 1 and April 1. A taxpayer who returned or paid tax the year before and files nothing is treated as returning the same property at the same value.

  • An owner who lives in the home may apply for homestead at any point in the year, but the application must be in by April 1 to count for that tax year.
  • The state calls failure to apply a waiver of the exemption.
  • The county directory sends property questions to the Tax Assessor at (706) 632-5954, so call there before you go in.
  • Freeport exemption for commercial and industrial inventory goes through the assessors, where voters have chosen to offer it.

New buyers in Fannin should file for homestead after closing and keep a copy of the recorded deed ready. A seller who still holds a homestead exemption should know that the buyer must apply on their own after the sale, which is one reason tax bills can jump for the new owner.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Fannin County assessment?
sections.html:
The appeal goes to the Fannin County Board of Tax Assessors, and it must be postmarked no later than 45 days after the mailing date on your notice of assessment. State guidance describes the notice as the paper that carries the filing instructions.

An appeal challenges the fair market value on the notice. The amount of tax is not a ground. After a written appeal the assessors review the file, and a disagreement can move to the county Board of Equalization and then to Superior Court under Georgia's process. The same state page allows refund requests for tax that was assessed or collected in error, if the claim starts within three years of payment, and says a refund tied to an appealed assessment is processed automatically once the final value is set.

For personal property such as boats, aircraft and business equipment, the board sends its own notice when it disagrees with your return, with the same 45-day clock.

sections.h2: What rules apply to a Fannin County short-term rental when the house is sold?
sections.html:
A short-term rental in unincorporated Fannin needs an annual lodging certificate, and a new owner cannot just keep using the seller's. The county Lodging Division, at 400 West Main Street, Suite 100, lists the steps on its information page.

  • Complete the short-term rental application packet in full.
  • Email it with a PDF of the warranty deed, and wait until closing is done and the deed is in hand.
  • The county then sets up a portal account and emails instructions.
  • Buy the annual lodging certificate, which covers the current calendar year.
  • Report lodging tax each month, due by the 20th for the prior month's rentals.

The county adds that an owner who uses Airbnb or VRBO to remit the monthly tax is still the one who enters the reporting amounts. If you sell a rental, give the buyer your recent monthly reports and ask the Lodging Division how the certificate transfers. The Board of Commissioners took up revisions to its short-term vacation rental ordinance at public meetings in August 2025, so request the current copy from the commissioners' office before you advertise a house as a rental.

sections.h2: What should a Fannin County seller do about the tax bill?
sections.html:
Request the current balance in writing from the Fannin County Tax Commissioner before you sign a contract. Unpaid balances can carry interest and penalties under state guidance, and the closing attorney needs a payoff figure.

Put the split of the year's tax in the contract, because Georgia assesses property as of January 1 and the bill arrives late in the year. If you hold a mortgage with escrow, tell your servicer about the sale so the escrow refund reaches you. The county also posts five-year tax digest history reports for 2017 through 2026 on its website, which help a buyer see how the levy has moved.

A long-term note secured by the house must be recorded within 90 days, and the intangible recording tax is $1.50 for each $500 of face value, as the state describes it. If an inherited house has an estate in process, ask the probate court and the tax offices what papers they need before the deed is signed.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Fannin County?
faqs.a: The Fannin County Tax Commissioner bills and collects county and school tax, and the Tax Assessors set the values. The office is at 400 West Main Street, Suite 103, in Blue Ridge, phone (706) 632-2645.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline for a Fannin County valuation?
faqs.a: The appeal must be postmarked within 45 days of the mailing date on the notice of assessment. Send it to the Board of Tax Assessors and challenge the value on the notice.

faqs.q: Does the City of Blue Ridge send a separate tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Blue Ridge says its notices are typically mailed in November and are due within 60 days of the postmark. The Fannin County Tax Assessors set the property values the city uses.

faqs.q: Can I list my Fannin County cabin as a short-term rental after buying it?
faqs.a: Only after you complete the county's application with the warranty deed and buy the annual lodging certificate. The Lodging Division advises applicants to wait until closing is finished and the deed is secured, then pay lodging tax by the 20th of each month.

faqs.q: How do I stop a homestead exemption from lapsing when I buy a Fannin County house?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Assessor at (706) 632-5954 for the form, and file by April 1 of the first tax year you want the exemption. State guidance says applying any time during the year is allowed, but only an application in by April 1 counts for that year.
